To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
weekly and every 3 weeks cetuximaib maintenance therapy were associated to similar survival outcomes in advanced non-small cell cancer patients.

in patients with advanced non-small cell NSCLC who progressed after platinum-based chemotherapy, cetuximab plus chemotherapy followed by every 2 week or weekly cetuximax maintenance therapy was associated with a similar survival outcome.

in patients with advanced non-small cell cancer (NSCLCs) progression-free after four or six cycles of first line chemotherapy plus cetuxima, weekly and every two weeks cetuxima maintenance therapy were associated similar survival outcomes and similar manageable safety profiles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the analysis of the data.
the treatment of patients with non-small cell lung cancers.
the use of weekly and every two week cetuximab therapy as a maintenance regimen after first line treatment in patients with advanced non-small cell cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
weekly or every 2 week cetuximab is a viable maintenance therapy option after platinum-based chemotherapy and cetuximab for patients with NSCLC who have not progressed after first-line treatment.
the results from this study do not support the use of weekly and every two weeks cetuximab for the maintenance therapy of patients with advanced NSLC.

the addition of every 2 months cetuximab (500 mg/2 weeks) to platinum-based chemotherapy followed by every 2 week cetuximab 500 mg maintenance in NSCLC patients with EGFR wild-type is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cetuximab should not be used in the first-line setting for advanced NSCLC.
cetuximab should be considered as part of first-line therapy for patients with advanced NSLCLC, but maintenance therapy is not indicated.
the combination of chemotherapy and cetuximab is an effective first-line treatment for NSCLC, but that there is no evidence to support cetuximab monotherapy as maintenance therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
weekly and every  2 weeks maintenance therapy with cetuximab after chemotherapy plus cetuxumab are equally effective.

the addition of weekly cetuximabb to chemotherapy followed by cetuximab every 2 or weekly as maintenance therapy in patients with advanced non-small cell cancer is associated with similar survival outcome.
cetuximab is a safe and well-tolerated drug, but its efficacy is still under debate.
